query: Eutectic high-entropy alloys contain dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries, where microcracking can initiate and lead to catastrophic damage during room-temperature tensile deformation. Conventional processing commonly raises strength at the expense of ductility, while the wide range of previously proposed microstructural-design and processing strategies has not eliminated room-temperature brittleness and limited tensile ductility. Under these constraints, what single intervention could improve both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility? State one testable hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline, defines its boundary conditions, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: A trace addition of Boron which segregates to the lamellar interfaces will enhance interfacial cohesion and delay microcrack initiation, thereby simultaneously increasing both yield strength and tensile ductility in eutectic high-entropy alloys.
generation.material_initial_state: A eutectic high-entropy alloy produced by conventional casting that exhibits dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries, where microcrack initiation at these interfaces causes room-temperature brittleness.
generation.intervention: Introduce a minor (~0.1–0.5 at.%) Boron addition during alloy synthesis to promote interfacial segregation at the lamella boundaries.
generation.conditions: After casting, perform a homogenizing solution treatment before room-temperature quasi-static tensile testing (strain rate ~10^(-4) s^(-1)) in ambient atmosphere.
generation.structural_mediator: Enhanced chemical bonding and reduced interface energy at the lamellar boundaries due to Boron segregation.
generation.mechanism: Boron atoms preferentially segregate to the dual-phase interfaces, which increases interfacial cohesion, reduces stress concentration sites, and promotes a finer, more uniform lamellar spacing. This modification delays microcrack nucleation while still supporting dislocation activity needed for ductility.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to the unmodified baseline alloy, the Boron-treated alloy is expected to show higher yield and ultimate tensile strengths along with improved elongation at fracture, indicating simultaneous enhancement in strength and ductility.
generation.baseline: Eutectic high-entropy alloys produced by conventional processing that display brittle tensile behavior due to microcrack initiation at unmodified lamellar interfaces.
generation.boundary: The beneficial effect is anticipated for alloys with a dual-phase lamellar colony structure produced via conventional casting and solution treatment. The influence of Boron may differ in other microstructural contexts or processing routes.
generation.uncertainty: The optimal Boron concentration and its exact segregation behavior at the interface remain uncertain, and the quantitative improvements in mechanical properties require experimental confirmation.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of alloy specimens with identical processing conditions: one set with the trace Boron addition and one without. Conduct identical homogenizing heat treatments followed by room-temperature quasi-static tensile testing. Use microscopy (SEM/TEM) and chemical analysis methods (e.g., SIMS) to confirm Boron segregation at the lamellar interfaces.
measurements: Tensile stress–strain curves (yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, elongation at fracture)
Microstructural imaging of lamellar colony interfaces
Chemical analysis confirming Boron segregation (e.g., SIMS or EDS mapping)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Boron-treated specimens do not show statistically significant improvements in both tensile strength and ductility compared to the baseline, or if chemical analyses do not confirm notable Boron segregation at the lamellar interfaces, the hypothesis will be considered falsified.
